conviction_note: Near non-result. Management said on 14 Sep that Q3 was tracking to a guide the consensus already sits on. The one company-level hint of upside is capital-markets fees running ahead of a guided -20% q/q. Against that, the 13-14 Oct peer tape was mixed to negative for commercial lenders (WFC -1.5%, BAC -4% premarket) and a September Fed hike lifted deposit costs. The stock is -15.9% since its July print with upside skew paid and only 1.8% short, so the lean is slight: p_up 54 on an abs move of 2.8 (between the 0.92% median reaction and an implied ~3.7-4.0% on a 71%-wide ATM spread). impact_sum is +0.2 and the scaled number is +0.22; the two agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 EPS consensus $4.88 (TickerLeague, 12 analysts, https://tickerleague.com/companies/PNC/estimates), $4.91 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PNC/earnings-forecasts) and $4.97-4.98 (Zacks/AAII, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/514996-what-you-need-to-know-about-the-pnc-financial-services-group-incs-q3-earnings). Revenue consensus is ~$6.60-6.61B. The company's 3Q26 guide (2Q26 slides, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026048308/a2q26earningsslides_vf.htm) has NII +3-3.5% on $4,107M (~$4,230-4,250M), fees -5-5.5% on $2,279M (~$2,155-2,165M), other income $150-200M (so revenue ~$6.54-6.62B), adjusted expense -2-3% on $3,837M (~$3,720-3,760M) and NCOs ~$225M. That gives guide-implied EPS of roughly $4.90-5.00, so the consensus sits at the guide midpoint. The bar is sourced to the guide plus agreeing estimates. The next-quarter bar: street 4Q26 NIM exit ~3.08% (Najarian on the Q2 call) against management's '>3% by year-end'. Implied 4Q NII from the FY guide (+15-15.5% on $14,410M) is roughly +0.6% to +2.3% q/q.
positioning_check: Short interest is 7,221,106 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, ~1.8% of ~398.9m shares, 3.47 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/pnc/short-interest, read 2026-10-14 via the sweep row): not crowded. 25d skew is -6.26 vol points (calls over puts, 'upside paid') and put/call OI is 1.1. The front-expiry straddle is 4.13% (event 4.02%) but the ATM spread is 71% of mid, so treat it as indicative; Unusual Whales quotes ±3.65%. The tape is -7.72% over 20 days, -16.9% from the 52-week high, and -15.9% since the 7/15 print against SPY +2.7% (AAII, 2026-10-14). The S&P Global headline says most US bank stocks traded lower in September after the 16 Sep Fed hike (median -3.5%, 15 of 203 positive; article itself 403).

findings.finding: At Barclays on 14 Sep 2026 (two weeks before quarter-end), CFO Reilly said FY26 and 3Q26 guidance were unchanged ('We expected a good third quarter, and we are tracking to it'). He said criticized assets have come down, NPAs and leading indicators are improving, spot deposits are growing faster than loans (mainly commercial), NIM will be 'above 3% by the end of the year', and every FirstBank financial target has been hit or exceeded. The consensus ($4.88-4.98) sits at the guide midpoint (~$4.90-5.00).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PNC's eight-print median reaction is 0.92% and 6 of 8 were up. The Q2 2026 beat ($4.85 vs ~$4.43) with a raised FY guide traded down ~3.8% early (deposits -1.7% and expenses in focus) and closed +0.9% in the baseline. Beats are damped.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, and the stock has fallen ~8% since that statement despite it, which suggests the sector tape (Fed hike, BofA's 'languish' call on 8 Oct) and not PNC's quarter drove the drawdown. If the 'tracking to guide' plus credit-improving message were fully priced, the stock would not be at -16% vs SPY since July with 6.3 points of upside skew. It sits inside the guide, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The deposit point addresses the Q2 deposit-decline concern from the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15271210600571904). Peer: JPM commercial client deposits +1% q/q and firmwide +2% q/q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfexhibit991narrative.htm). Same speaker and document as finding 2; the facts differ.

findings.finding: Capital-markets/advisory fees look set to beat a conservative q/q guide. On the Q2 call Reilly guided capital markets and advisory fees 'down about 20% quarter over quarter' in 3Q after a record Q2, which is built into the -5% to -5.5% total fee guide ($2,279M base). At Barclays on 14 Sep he said capital markets is 'having a record year' and Harris Williams is 'having yet again another record year'. JPM's 3Q IB fees were +14% y/y and only -8% q/q, and GS beat on equities. Each $40M of fee upside is ~$0.08 EPS (~1.6% of the bar).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 a fee beat (+10% q/q, record capital markets) came with a sold-early reaction that closed +0.9%. No line-level attribution was found for earlier prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue ($6.60-6.61B) sits at the guide midpoint (~$6.58B), so the street has not visibly lifted fees for the Barclays 'record year' comment or the JPM/GS IB read-through. If it had, consensus revenue would sit above the guide's top (~$6.62B) and EPS above $5.00. It is an inference from a qualitative company comment plus peer proxies, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: JPM IB fees +14% y/y, -8% q/q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfexhibit991narrative.htm, 2026-10-13). GS equities strength (https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/). The Barclays comment is the same document as finding 1.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp on 16 Sep 2026 to 3.75-4.00%, against a PNC guide that assumed stable rates all year. Demchak said NII is roughly neutral to ±25bp, and Reilly guided the deposit rate paid up '5 basis points or so'. A regional peer that reported on 13 Oct (FB Financial) saw its NIM fall 12bp q/q (3.95% to 3.83%) on 'higher funding costs relative to earning asset yields', with interest-bearing deposit cost rising 7bp. The risk is a softer-than-street 4Q NII/NIM guide against the 3.08% street NIM exit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WFC fell ~5% in July 2025 on an NII outlook cut despite a beat (peer, not PNC). No PNC-specific NII-guide surprise reaction was sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public and bank stocks sold off after it (S&P Global), so the macro part is priced. What is not visible is whether PNC's funding cost rose more than its 5bp guide. If the street had cut for it, 4Q NIM expectations would sit nearer 3.00% than 3.08%. It is a proxy from a small Tennessee bank, and PNC's management says it is rate-neutral with fixed-rate asset repricing 'constructive' into 2027, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The Q2 call says NII is neutral to 25bp and guidance assumed stable rates (https://www.webull.com/news/15271210600571904). That cuts against this finding and is why the finding is small. ClaritX (2026-10-06) also covers the hike and margin pressure (https://www.claritx.ai/blog/q3-2026-earnings-kickoff-big-banks-economy).

findings.finding: PNC enters the print -15.9% since its 15 Jul report against SPY +2.7% (AAII, 14 Oct), -7.7% over 20 days and -16.9% from its 52-week high, after US bank stocks broadly fell in September following the 16 Sep hike. That is a sector move, not a PNC disclosure: the guide was reaffirmed on 14 Sep. Short interest is 1.8% and options pay for upside (skew -6.26), so a guide-in-line print meets a depressed price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print came after a run-up and was sold early ('more sellers than buyers', Demchak). The January 2026 print, after a weaker tape, gained +3.79%. Q3 2025, during the regional-credit scare, fell -3.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The upside skew already says the market expects relief, which is why this is sized small. Not priced would mean the consensus or price targets had been cut to match the 16% drawdown. Instead consensus EPS has been flat to up (1 down, 2 up revisions in the last month, per AAII) and the guide is reaffirmed, so the multiple and not the estimate absorbed the fall.
findings.independence: S&P Global, 'Most US bank stocks trade lower in September' (https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/articles/2026/10/most-us-bank-stocks-trade-lower-in-september-106462675, 403, title and snippet only). BofA 'regional banks could continue to languish', 2026-10-08 (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/regional-bank-stocks-could-continue-to-languish-amid-macro-headwinds-bofa-says-ce785ddfda81f125). That is a sector-negative counterpoint, already in the price.

findings.finding: Peer reactions on 13-14 Oct were mixed to negative for commercial and consumer lenders. WFC beat EPS ($1.87) but fell ~1.5% (NII +$200M q/q). C beat and dipped 0.7%. JPM missed EPS ($5.57 vs $5.91, its first miss in ~3 years) and was +0.8%, with a $539M reserve build mostly in wholesale. BAC on 14 Oct missed revenue ($29.96B vs $30.56B, adjusted EPS $1.08 vs $1.10) with a $1.2B regulatory charge and was ~-4% premarket. Dimon flagged 'sticky inflation… rising interest rates'. The tape is selling bank beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PNC's Q2 2026 beat was sold early in a similar 'beats sold' bank tape (Citi -4% to -5% on its Q2 beat on 14 Jul 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the peer moves happened before PNC's spot was sealed (13:59 UTC 14 Oct, after BAC's premarket). What remains is the reaction function, that a beat at PNC may be sold the way WFC's and C's were. BAC's drop is largely idiosyncratic (the regulatory charge), so the read-through is small.
findings.independence: BAC results and reaction (https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/stockstory-2026-10-14-bank-of-america-nysebac-misses-q3-2026-revenue-estimates). JPM reserve build (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfexhibit991narrative.htm).

findings.finding: Evercore ISI kept Outperform but cut its PNC price target to $265 from $285 around 1 Oct 2026, citing caution on expenses and asset quality (single aggregator source; the $285 prior target is not verified elsewhere).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a sell-side view already on the wire, so it is largely priced. It is filed because 'expenses and asset quality' are the two lines where PNC's Q2 drew criticism, and Reilly's 14 Sep 'investing at a pretty good clip' leaves room for an expense guide above the street.
findings.independence: Expense concern in the Q2 reaction (https://www.chartmill.com/news/external/78606/pnc-financial-q2-earnings-top-on-nii-fee-income-growth-stock-down). Asset quality is contradicted by Reilly's 14 Sep 'criticized assets have come down' (finding 1), hence the small size.

findings.finding: Capital return: Reilly guided 3Q26 repurchases to 'approximate the same level' as Q2's $610M, the dividend was raised 18% to $2.00 (record date 14 Oct), and CET1 was 9.9%. The ROTCE exit-rate target of 18% for 4Q26 is unchanged (Q2 17.9%).
findings.why_not_priced: Already guided and in the share count the consensus uses. It moves only if 4Q buyback guidance steps up. Sized at 0.
findings.independence: Same Q2 call as findings 2 and 3. 2Q26 slides (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026048308/a2q26earningsslides_vf.htm).

Regional peers (M&T, Fifth Third, Commerce, Regions) 3Q26 results before 14 Oct: none found other than FB Financial

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive and agree with the upside-paid skew (-6.26) and the -7.7% run-up, so the lean is probably partly priced. The peer tape selling bank beats cuts against it, which keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the 'tracking to guide' finding lands inside what the company guided, so it is cut from +0.4 to +0.2.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): PNC's beats are damped (median 0.92%, Q2 beat sold early), so the capital-markets fee finding is cut from +0.5 to +0.4.

Lesson 7 (positioning): the drawdown/relief finding agrees with the upside skew, so it is probably partly priced; cut from +0.4 to +0.3. Short interest was checked before the negatives (1.8%, not crowded), so the negatives are unchanged.
p_up moved from 55 to 54 because the bar sits at the guide midpoint and the lean agrees with the skew.
